limitations: Actual compiled Game pointer handler, three native HTML-video samples 120 ms apart, production sharpness selection/JPEG crop, native RTC data channel, real matcher and actual sidebar.

Only source media and signaling are adapted: deterministic 1920x1080 SNAPTEST canvas MediaStream tracks and loopback memory signaling; no physical camera, microphone, real room, STUN, TURN or remote NAT.

Recognition models/index are warmed. Frame crop is encoded at production JPEG quality 0.9, which differs from supplied-image SNAPTEST quality 0.62; the resulting input is not pixel-identical to that benchmark.

Fresh clears only the test Game's room-hint ref before the actual pointer click. Prior cards can still warm reference caches. Immediate repeats keep the newly verified hint; this does not measure first-visit downloads.
Paint is approximated by decoded image pixels at full ancestor opacity plus the following requestAnimationFrame; this does not measure physical screen scanout.

The canvas camera composites each source scene onto opaque black before every repaint. Transparent playmat pixels must not accumulate through repeated source-over draws; each static camera frame therefore has the same pixels.

Each source scene is exported losslessly with its exact click metadata; --sceneFixtures replays those same pixels for the other arm. Native JPEG hashes must still match before comparing accuracy or latency.

Baseline freezes application source at the requested Git revision; both arms intentionally serve the same current working catalog. Manifest/cards SHA256 and Milo model/gallery IDs are recorded separately.

controlInstrumentation.purpose: Loopback test-only sampling, source-painter, owner/worker events, first/final SHA and held detector reply instrumentation. Production source fingerprints remain recorded separately.
